title: How You Ask Shapes What You Get: A Theory-Seeded Measurement of Articulation in Advice-Seeking LLM Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2608.29591v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Users articulate the same advice-seeking request in different ways: some specify detailed constraints, others gesture at a vague need. Prior work treats this variation as noise to be averaged away; we instead treat it as a stable, measurable structure in the input distribution. We ask whether articulation (how people ask) forms latent dimensions separable from topic (what they ask about), and whether it is associated with how language models respond. We extract interpretable features from 16,447 advice-seeking prompts pooled from public chat corpora (WildChat, LMSYS, and ShareChat) and recover a small set of latent articulation factors that replicate across train/test splits and across corpora. Because this structure is largely separable from topic, the populations it defines cut across topics and stay invisible to topic- or task-based evaluation. translated_title: 你如何提问决定你得到什么：基于理论种子的大语言模型建议寻求对话中表述方式的测量
translated_abstract: 用户以不同的方式表述相同的建议寻求请求：有些人指定详细的约束条件，而另一些人只是模糊地表达需求。先前的工作将这种差异视为需要被平均掉的噪声；我们则将其视为输入分布中一种稳定、可测量的结构。我们探究表述方式（人们如何提问）是否形成了与主题（他们问什么）可分离的潜在维度，以及它是否与语言模型的响应方式相关联。我们从汇集自公共聊天语料库（WildChat、LMSYS 和 ShareChat）的 16,447 条建议寻求提示中提取可解释的特征，并恢复出一小组潜在的表述因子，这些因子在训练/测试划分以及不同语料库之间均能复现。由于这种结构在很大程度上与主题可分离，它所定义的用户群体跨越各个主题，并且在基于主题或任务的评估中保持不可见。这些因子定义了少数几种反复出现的表述风格，其中一种尤为突出：（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次将“如何提问”（表述方式）作为与“问什么”（主题）可分离的稳定潜在结构进行测量，从三个公共语料库的 16,447 条建议寻求提示中提取可解释特征并恢复出可复现的潜在表述因子，揭示了这种结构会影响语言模型的响应却被现有基于主题或任务的评估所忽视。
en_tdlr: This study treats articulation (how users ask) as a stable, measurable latent structure separable from topic, recovering replicable articulation factors from 16,447 advice-seeking prompts across three public chat corpora, and showing that this structure shapes LLM responses yet remains invisible to topic- or task-based evaluation.
